test_title: PYST 27: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - Mathematics (Held On: 20 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: maths
question: A can lay a railway track between two stations in 22 days, and B can complete the same task in 10 days. With C's help, they finish the job in just 2 days. In how many days can C complete the job alone?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let Total Work = LCM of 22, 10, and 2 = 110 units.

Combined efficiency of A + B + C = 110 ÷ 2 = 55 units/day.

Efficiency of A = 110 ÷ 22 = 5 units/day.

Efficiency of B = 110 ÷ 10 = 11 units/day.

Efficiency of C = 55 − (5 + 11) = 39 units/day.

Time taken by C alone = 110 ÷ 39 = 2³²/₃₉ days.

**∴ The correct answer is 2³²/₃₉ days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A = 22 days

Time taken by B = 10 days

Time taken by A, B and C together = 2 days

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of A + B + C = 55

⇒ Efficiency of A = 5

⇒ Efficiency of B = 11

⇒ Efficiency of C = Total Efficiency − (Efficiency of A + Efficiency of B)

⇒ Efficiency of C = 55 − (5 + 11)

⇒ Efficiency of C = 55 − 16 = 39 units/day

⇒ Time taken by C alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of C

⇒ Time taken by C alone = 110 ÷ 39 = 2³²/₃₉ days

**∴ The correct answer is 2³²/₃₉ days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns

Works exactly like Time & Work, but filling pipes have positive efficiency and emptying pipes have negative efficiency.

Work & Wages

Wages are always distributed in the direct ratio of the total work done by each person. If the time worked is the same, wages are distributed in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Alternate Day Work

Find the total work done in a complete cycle (e.g., 2 days for 2 people). Determine how many full cycles fit into the total work and add the remaining work for the next day's turn.
